question: Question linked to image nº10 A 80-year-old woman with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia and cervical osteoarthritis treated with enalapril / hydrochlorothiazide and simvastatin for years and sporadic with paracetamol. Consultation for pruritic skin lesions on trunk and extremities of 2 weeks of evolution for which no medical treatment has been performed (Image). The patient is hemodynamically stable and afebrile when she goes to the emergency department. Point out the correct option:

options.opa: In the skin biopsy performed of a recent lesion appearance, I would expect to find epidermal spongiosis, spongiosa vesicles and an eosinophilic infiltrate.
options.opb: The lesions are compatible with generalized acute exanthematous pustulosis, which is why he would initiate oral treatment with amoxicillin / clavulanic acid.
options.opc: With the suspicion of an autoimmune bullous disease, a biopsy of the lesions is performed for direct immunofluorescence. Hospital admission is made and treatment with prednisone is started at a dose of 1mg / kg / day.
options.opd: With the suspicion of disseminated eczema, a lesion biopsy was performed for hematoxylin-eosin and treatment with prednisone was started at a dose of 1mg / kg / day.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Chronic use of enalapril/hydrochlorothiazide and simvastatin -> potential drug-induced skin reactions -> pruritic skin lesions on trunk and extremities -> 80% CHAIN: Pruritic skin lesions on trunk and extremities -> possible allergic reaction or dermatitis -> skin biopsy for further evaluation -> 70% CHAIN: Skin biopsy of lesions -> histopathological findings of epidermal spongiosis, spongiosa vesicles, and eosinophilic infiltrate -> suggestive of allergic contact dermatitis or eczema -> 75% CHAIN: Lesions compatible with generalized acute exanthematous pustulosis -> consider infectious etiology -> initiation of oral treatment with amoxicillin/clavulanic acid -> 60% CHAIN: Suspicion of autoimmune bullous disease -> lesion biopsy for direct immunofluorescence -> hospital admission -> treatment with prednisone at 1mg/kg/day -> 70% CHAIN: Suspicion of disseminated eczema -> lesion biopsy for hematoxylin-eosin -> treatment with prednisone at 1mg/kg/day -> 80%
enhanced_information: Chronic use of enalapril/hydrochlorothiazide and simvastatin can lead to potential drug-induced skin reactions, presenting as pruritic skin lesions on trunk and extremities. Skin biopsy may show epidermal spongiosis, spongiosa vesicles, and eosinophilic infiltrate, suggestive of allergic contact dermatitis or eczema. The lesions are not compatible with generalized acute exanthematous pustulosis or autoimmune bullous disease. Treatment with prednisone at 1mg/kg/day for suspected disseminated eczema is appropriate.
analysis: The patient's presentation with pruritic skin lesions and a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and medication use suggests a drug reaction or an underlying autoimmune condition. Given the lack of fever and hemodynamic stability, a drug reaction is more likely. The absence of vesicles and eosinophilic infiltrate makes generalized acute exanthematous pustulosis less likely. Autoimmune bullous diseases are a consideration but less common in this context. Disseminated eczema is a possibility, but the lack of specific features mentioned in the question makes it less likely.
